Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates hyperlucency and decreased vascular markings in the right lung field, which are classic signs of chronic pulmonary artery obstruction (often resulting in oligemia). This finding is consistent with the known complications of Takayasu arteritis affecting the pulmonary arteries, rather than an acute embolic event or other options listed.
